4 runbook chunk(s) for 'SITE_DOWN link aggregation router fiber transport failure', best first (excerpts):
[RB-FIBER-CUT#03] Fiber cut on a transport link > Differential diagnosis: ... If a window covers the link (or the aggregation router above it) and the outage sits inside the window, it is expected and not an incident. ... Versus a site power failure ... A degraded microwave link keeps its sites up. ... Check `nodes.attrs.medium`: a microwave link can also fail hard, and the data then looks like a fiber cut, although the repair is different. ...
[RB-FIBER-CUT#01] Fiber cut on a transport link > Overview: A transport link (node type `transport_link`, id like `LNK-XXX-NN-A`) carries all the traffic of the sites behind it, usually three to five. When the fiber is cut, or the optic or port on the link fails, every one of those sites loses its backhaul at the same moment. The sites themselves are healthy. ... Repairs take from about two hours to most of a working day.
[RB-FIBER-CUT#05] Fiber cut on a transport link > Verification steps: 1. `get_alarms` for the two hours around the first drop: find `LINK_LOS` on a link and list the `SITE_DOWN` sites. ... `get_topology` for that link: confirm the `SITE_DOWN` set equals the children of the link, no more and no fewer. ... `get_maintenance` for the link, its sites and the aggregation router, around the onset. ... Read `cleared_at` on the link alarm for the rest...
[RB-MICROWAVE-DEGRADATION#03] Microwave link degradation > Differential diagnosis: Versus the harmless background LINK_DEGRADED ... Versus a fiber cut ... Degradation keeps availability high and has no `SITE_DOWN`. If the link is fiber, rain fade cannot be the explanation. Versus a fiber link starting to fail On a fiber link, a minor `LINK_DEGRADED` with falling optical power can precede a cut by up to an hour. ... Check `get_changes` for the link and its sites.
Excerpts are cut; search again with a narrower query for the rest.

result.markdown:
# Transport Failure Impacting Sfax Sites

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** transport_failure at `LNK-SFX-01-B`
- **Confidence:** high (Direct alarms observed on the affected link and child sites, timing fits the KPI drops exactly, and maintenance, changes, and external events were checked and ruled out.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-27 08:00 to 2026-09-27 10:24
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-27 08:04
- **Affected:** S-SFX-005, S-SFX-008, S-SFX-010

## Summary

Fiber link failure on LNK-SFX-01-B causing simultaneous SITE_DOWN alarms across dependent sites in Sfax.

Traffic dropped across Sfax sites S-SFX-005, S-SFX-008, and S-SFX-010 due to a transport link failure starting at 2026-09-27 08:04 and recovering at 2026-09-27 10:24 when all alarms cleared.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-27 08:00: Anomaly detector alert active_users and availability drop begins for Sfax sites [ALR-0033]
- 2026-09-27 08:04: Critical SITE_DOWN alarm raised on S-SFX-005 [ALM-000550]
- 2026-09-27 08:04: Critical SITE_DOWN alarm raised on S-SFX-010 [ALM-000551]
- 2026-09-27 08:04: Critical SITE_DOWN alarm raised on S-SFX-008 [ALM-000552]
- 2026-09-27 10:23: SITE_DOWN alarm cleared on S-SFX-005 and S-SFX-008 [ALM-000550, ALM-000552]
- 2026-09-27 10:24: SITE_DOWN alarm cleared on S-SFX-010 [ALM-000551]

## Evidence

- Detector alert ALR-0033 showed active users and availability drops on S-SFX-005, S-SFX-008, and S-SFX-010 starting around 2026-09-27 08:00. [ALR-0033]
- Critical SITE_DOWN alarms were triggered simultaneously at 2026-09-27 08:04 for S-SFX-005, S-SFX-010, and S-SFX-008, all of which depend on fiber link LNK-SFX-01-B. [T2, T4, ALM-000550, ALM-000551, ALM-000552]
- No maintenance windows were scheduled on the affected sites or their parents during the incident window. [T3]
- No configuration changes were performed on the affected nodes or their parents during the window. [T6]
- No external events were reported for the SFX region during the incident timeframe. [T9]

## Hypotheses

1. **transport_failure** at LNK-SFX-01-B: confirmed. Simultaneous SITE_DOWN alarms across all child sites of LNK-SFX-01-B without any simultaneous changes or maintenance confirm a transport link failure. [T2, T4, ALM-000550, ALM-000551, ALM-000552]
2. **planned_maintenance**: rejected. Maintenance query returned no scheduled maintenance for the affected nodes. [T3]
3. **bad_change**: rejected. Change management query returned no changes on the affected nodes or their parents during the incident window. [T6]

## Ruled out

- ALM-000553: Warning TEMP_HIGH on S-SFX-002 occurred later on 2026-09-27 11:40, well after the traffic drop and resolution of the Sfax transport incident.
- ALM-000554: Warning TEMP_HIGH on S-SFX-002 occurred later on 2026-09-27 11:50, irrelevant to the morning traffic drop.
- ALR-0034: Ongoing alert starting on 2026-09-28 08:45 on site S-SFX-003 falls outside the scope of yesterday morning's traffic drop.

## Recommended actions

- Inspect fiber link LNK-SFX-01-B for physical damage or transient cuts.
- Review aggregation router logs for LNK-SFX-01-B interface stability.

truth.notes: trap=missing_alarm; Fibre cut on LNK-SFX-01-B; all 3 downstream sites lost service until repair. The LINK_LOS alarm was never raised: only SITE_DOWN alarms on the sites exist. Trap: there is no alarm on LNK-SFX-01-B, only 3 SITE_DOWN alarms on sites, so a hasty investigator names a site or a set of independent site faults. Settled by: get_topology shows that the 3 sites share the parent LNK-SFX-01-B and that nothing else hangs under it; they went down in the same minute and sites on sibling links stayed up, so the shared link is the one cause.
